rationale: Whether an SDF shape emits a stroke chart is decided by a switch on an enum and needs no renderer, but the predicate and its message lived inside the Skia-only translation unit while the non-Skia stub dropped the shape argument entirely. The same call therefore answered differently per build, and a non-GPU build skipped a check it could perform. This moves the predicate, the shape name and the message into an unconditionally compiled unit that both backends consult — the rule sksl_declares_uniform() already follows in the same file so the two backends agree. Only genuine SkSL compilation stays Skia-gated. No API is added or removed, no authority boundary moves, no alternate renderer appears, and the with-Skia answer is unchanged. Pulp-only because Pulp still builds and ships this implementation independently and there is no counterpart Vellum commit to backport from.
tests: pulp-test-canvas SDF chart refuses and names every shape it cannot chart
